data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when the subject's failure mode is independent of the test's installation; the 1/9 result is the only case where the test's guard was absent, so the test described the mutation rather than constraining it, while the 4/4 to 6/7 results show constraint because the guards were already installed.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a mutation in an ordinarily-guarded module survived, the guard-presence explanation would be falsified.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py had a hidden guard that was not in the record, the 1/9 result would be a constraint case.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the distribution were uniform across all modules, the guard-presence hypothesis would be unnecessary.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The distribution is explained by guard presence: where a guard exists, the test constrains the mutation by requiring the guard to hold; where no guard exists, the test describes the mutation by failing regardless of the mutation's content. The 1/9 loss is the description case.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
